deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page (question 16) asks whether, for a non-trivial 'contracteur' A, the functors i_A : A^ → Cat (X ↦ A/X) and j_A : Cat → A^ induce mutually inverse equivalences after localising by weak equivalences ('homotopismes'). In later terminology this asks whether A is a test category, so that A^ is a modelizing topos. This page is a short answer and caveat in the vocabulary of Pursuing Stacks (1983).

(1) Claim: a strictly locally aspheric topos need not be modelizing, even when it has the form A^. Equivalently, A need not be a test category. The hypothesis on A is the one later called 'totalement asphérique': A is aspheric and products of representables are aspheric.

(2) Counterexample recipe: take A with finite products. Then A has a final object, and products of representables are representable, hence aspheric, so A is totally aspheric and A^ is strictly locally aspheric. Then add a degeneracy condition. The surviving text says the final object of A has exactly one section; the crossed-out drafts say the final object is also initial (a zero object). The crossed-out example 'à corps résiduel k' points to local k-algebras with residue field k, or their duals: pointed infinitesimal k-schemes, where Spec k is a zero object.

Why a zero object, or more generally an initial object 0, kills modelizingness:
- For any presheaf X, the full subcategory of A/X over 0 is the discrete set X(0).
- The functor r(a,x) = (0, x|_0) maps A/X onto this discrete set, with r∘incl = id.
- There is a natural transformation r ⇒ id, given by the maps 0 → a.
- Hence A/X is homotopy equivalent to the discrete set X(0).
- So weak equivalences in A^ are exactly the maps bijective on X(0), and Hot_A ≃ Set ≠ Hot. A is not even a weak test category.

The extreme example is A ≅ Δ_0 (the point), where A^ = Set.

(3) Positive statement: if A is a contractor ('contracteur', not 'contractante'), then A is a test category unless A ≅ Δ_0. This answers question 16 of the previous page. A contractor here means, roughly, a category with finite products whose objects are contractible via an interval in A. The phrase 'non trivial' in q.16 is exactly the exclusion A ≇ Δ_0. Presumably the mechanism is that a non-trivial contractor supplies a separating aspheric interval, and total asphericity plus such an interval gives a (strict) test category. That is the Pursuing Stacks criterion.

The marginal insertion at the top seems to strengthen (1): even if A is aspheric / A^ is equivalent in some sense to Cat, it can fail. It is too illegible to use.
errors: The surviving (non-crossed) hypothesis 'the final object of A has exactly one section' is either trivially true (Hom(e,e) is a singleton) or, read as 'every object has exactly one point', not by itself sufficient. Non-test-ness follows cleanly only from the crossed-out version (final object also initial, or more generally an initial object). The draft visibly struggles here.

The page asserts that every non-trivial contractor is a test category without proof. The needed step (existence of a separating aspheric interval and total asphericity) depends on the precise definition of 'contracteur', which is not given on the page.

ideas.what: A^ with A totally aspheric (e.g. A with finite products) is a strictly locally aspheric topos but need not be modelizing; A need not be a test category.
ideas.modern_name: totally aspheric categories vs. (strict) test categories
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (sections on locally aspheric / modelizing topoi and strict test categories)

ideas.what: A category with an initial (or zero) object has homotopy theory on presheaves equivalent to Set (A/X ≃ discrete X(0)), so it is never a test category. Δ_0 is the trivial case.
ideas.modern_name: categories with initial object are not (weak) test categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in test-category theory (Grothendieck, Maltsiniotis, Cisinski)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses Δ_0 not being a test category; the general initial-object remark is unsure

ideas.what: Every non-trivial contractor (category with finite products and contractible objects) is a test category.
ideas.modern_name: contractors / totally aspheric categories with separating interval are strict test categories

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early draft of material that appears in Pursuing Stacks: modelizing and locally aspheric topoi, contractors as test categories, Δ_0 as the trivial exception. The 'local k-algebras with residue field k' zero-object example is a nice concrete touch but trivial mathematically. The page is mainly of dating interest: it shows test-category questions in a list whose archive date is 'à partir de 1973'.

'telles que' → 'telle que' (refers to the category A)
'Tous [?] produit [?] cat [?] que A est équiv. à Δ_0' → most likely 'Par exemple le cas où A est équiv. à Δ_0'
'si A est une contractante [?]' → 'si A est un contracteur' (matching 'contracteur' on the previous page)
'il est cat. test, sauf si A ≅ Δ_0' is correct; the symbol is ≅ / ≃ (equivalence) with Δ_0
